$comment: DR-5 / G1 policy data for servers/exarchos-mcp/scripts/cli-derivation-guard.ts —
command names tolerated as hand-written string literals in the CLI composition root.
Every file named in this comment must be a repo-relative path that EXISTS: the guard
refuses to read this policy otherwise. (An earlier revision pointed at a
cli-derivation-seam module that had been renamed away, so the pointer a future author
follows led nowhere. The reference is bound now rather than merely corrected.)
This ships EMPTY on purpose. On introduction the guard reports all 11 literals
currently in servers/exarchos-mcp/src/adapters/cli.ts (doctor, version, feedback,
schema, topology, emissions, mcp, onboard, init, merge-orchestrate,
install-skills) rather than blessing them, so the guard's first run states the
real size of the debt instead of reporting green over it.
Populating this list, and enforcing that it may only ever SHRINK (an entry may
leave, none may arrive), is a separate deliverable and is deliberately not
implemented by the guard yet. Until then the guard reads this file but nothing
ratchets it.
KILL FIXTURE — DO NOT ADD 'merge-orchestrate' HERE. It is the guard's live
failing subject: merge_orchestrate is declared BOTH as a registry action (with
posture: 'shared-mutating') and by hand in servers/exarchos-mcp/src/adapters/cli.ts.
An earlier revision of this policy allowlisted it, which neutralized the exact
rejection DR-5 requires. The guard now REFUSES to read this file at all if the name
appears (see KILL_FIXTURE_COMMANDS in
servers/exarchos-mcp/scripts/cli-derivation-guard.ts). The remedy is to delete the
hand-written .command('merge-orchestrate') call, never to exempt it.
